How it works

A process with no surprises

Three stages, agreed scope, and clear checkpoints before anything moves forward.

  1. Step 01

    Discovery

    We define who the film is for, where it runs and what they should do next. I write the brief, shot list and schedule, confirm locations and permits, and agree the exact deliverables before anyone travels.

  2. Step 02

    Production

    Shoot day, run lean. Coverage is captured with the edit in mind — interviews, B-roll, cutaways and handles — so the sequence assembles instead of fighting the footage.

  3. Step 03

    Delivery + Revisions

    Rough cut within 48 hours, then two structured revision rounds covering edit, grade, sound mix and captions. Final masters arrive in 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 with captions burned in.

What clients say

FAQ

Questions I'm asked most

How do revisions work?

Two rounds are included on every project. You leave timecoded notes in a shared review link, I turn them around within one business day, and we agree in writing when the round is closed. Changing the brief after the rough cut — new structure, extra film, reshoots — is quoted before I touch it.

What is the typical turnaround?

Rough cut within 48 hours of the final shoot day is standard for brand films. Event highlights go out within 72 hours. Full delivery with grade, sound mix and all aspect ratios usually lands five to seven working days after the rough cut is approved.

Do you travel for shoots?

Yes — the whole UK is covered, and I regularly work in Ireland and the EU. Travel and accommodation are quoted transparently as a line item, never buried in the production fee.

Who owns the footage?

You do. Every package includes the graded master files and a copy of the full rushes on a shared drive. Camera originals are archived for 90 days after delivery in case something needs revisiting.

Can you work with our existing footage?

Often the best-value project there is. Send a sample of the archive, I will tell you honestly whether it can carry the story, and we proceed on an edit-only basis if it can.
